title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (variations on the 'loop equation'). An element u of N_{0,3}^{!~} is an automorphism-type datum acting on the profinite fundamental group \hat\Pi_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} and on its 'tilde' variant; effective (e.g. Galois) automorphisms are the main example. The previous page attached to u two things:
- a pair (α,β) in \hat\Pi_{0,3}^~ and \hat\Pi_{0,3} satisfying the loop relation (relation des lacets), determined only up to the \hat Z-action (α,β) ↦ (ℓ_0^u α, ℓ_0^u β), with ℓ_0 the loop around 0;
- 'adelic invariants' Θ = (μ,c,d,t,u) subject to congruences (88)/(89), and, for effective u, a lift f ∈ SL(2,\hat Z)' defined modulo f ↦ ℓ_0^n f.

This page.
1. Grothendieck notes that the invariants Θ, even together with f, are too weak to reconstruct the element \underline{\underline u} = φ(u) = u_{α,β,f} of GL(2,\hat Z)'. Read in modern terms, this is the image of u in the automorphisms attached to the genus-1 / SL_2 level, i.e. the action on the profinite completion of Γ_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z).
2. His reformulation:
   - Fix Θ. The set T = T_Θ of pairs (α,β) ≡ (1,1) mod 2 satisfying the conditions of the proposition is a \hat Z-torsor.
   - Let \hat Z act diagonally on T × SL(2,\hat Z) by (α,β,f) ↦ (ℓ_0^{-u}α, ℓ_0^{-u}β, ℓ_0^{-u}f) and pass to the quotient.
   - The quotient is the contracted product \check T_Θ ∧^{\hat Z} SL(2,\hat Z), where \check T is the opposite torsor and \hat Z acts on SL(2,\hat Z) by left multiplication by powers of ℓ_0. This is a right SL(2,\hat Z)-torsor.
   - A point of it determines \underline{\underline u} = u_{α,β,f}, up to the sign ambiguity f ↦ f·(−1), with −1 central.
3. He then judges these formulations 'not enthusing'. He decides (continued on the next page) that one must introduce explicitly the adelic group of all triples (α,β,f) satisfying the loop relation, together with the canonical homomorphism from M_{0,3}^{!~} into it.

Modern reading: the problem is to rigidify the Galois/automorphism action on the genus-0, 3-point and genus-1, 1-point levels compatibly. The torsor bookkeeping is replaced by a single group of compatible triples (genus-0 data α,β plus an SL_2-component f). That group is a precursor of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group \hat{GT} (Drinfeld's pairs (λ,f)) and of its genus-one extensions acting on \hat Γ_{1,1}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The torsor construction is the standard contracted product: since T is a \hat Z-torsor, T ×^{\hat Z} SL(2,\hat Z) is indeed a right SL(2,\hat Z)-torsor.

Minor imprecision: the twist uses the opposite torsor \check T because of the left/right conventions of the diagonal action. Also, the sign ambiguity (f vs −f) is only asserted, not justified; it presumably reflects the passage between SL(2,\hat Z) and GL(2,\hat Z)', or the centre ±1.

ideas.what: Attaching to a Galois-type automorphism of \hat\Pi_{0,3} a pair (α,β) satisfying the loop equation, well defined only up to a \hat Z-torsor of conjugations by powers of the loop ℓ_0
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT-elements (λ,f) up to inertia conjugation / tangential base point ambiguity
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action on \hat\pi_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}), but not these explicit torsors

ideas.what: Encoding the residual ambiguity as a contracted product \check T_Θ ∧^{\hat Z} SL(2,\hat Z), a right SL(2,\hat Z)-torsor
ideas.where_published: general torsor formalism (SGA, Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne)

ideas.what: Decision to define the adelic group of all triples (α,β,f) satisfying the loop relation, with a canonical homomorphism from the automorphism group M_{0,3}^{!~} to it
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group \hat{GT} and its genus-one / SL_2 extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (\hat{GT}); Nakamura–Schneps and others for genus 1; Enriquez for elliptic associators
ideas.where_published: Spirit of it in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); explicit group not published by Grothendieck

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans an explicit 'adelic group' of triples (α,β,f) mixing genus-0 loop-equation data with an SL(2,\hat Z)-component, plus a homomorphism from the automorphism group into it. This is a combined genus-0/genus-1 version of \hat{GT} in his own normalisation. It predates Drinfeld, and its exact definition may differ from the later Nakamura–Schneps-type definitions.
missed.quote: il faudra introduire explicitement et étudier ... le groupe adélique formé par les systèmes (α, β, f) satisfaisant à la relation des lacets
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's definition, including the f-component in SL(2,\hat Z)', with the genus-one GT variants (Nakamura–Schneps \hat Γ_{1,1}, Enriquez's elliptic GT) could clarify the history and possibly suggest a different normalisation. It is, however, largely anticipated by the later literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is historically interesting: an explicit pre-Drinfeld move toward a group of (α,β,f)-triples mixing P^1-{0,1,∞} and SL_2 data. But the mathematics here is torsor bookkeeping, and the target notion is now well known as GT and its genus-1 analogues.
transcription_corrections: 'λ^{-n}' should read 'ℓ_0^{-u}' (Grothendieck writes l_0 with exponent, as on the previous page).
'μ, c, d, t, n' should likely be 'μ, c, d, t, u', matching Θ=(μ,c,d,t,u) on the previous page.
'soit T = T_θ' is more likely 'soit T = T_Θ' (subscript Θ), and the phrase is 'on fait opérer alors \hat Z diagonalement'.
'quitte à changer de signe ou f est remplacé par (f(-1))' should read 'où f est remplacé par f(−1)', i.e. f·(−1).
